Class StreamPowerErosionEngine

java.lang.Object
org.ether.society.core.engine.AbstractSimulationEngine
org.ether.society.engines.tier1.StreamPowerErosionEngine
All Implemented Interfaces:
SimulationEngineModule
public class StreamPowerErosionEngine extends AbstractSimulationEngine
Stream Power Fluvial Erosion & Bagnold Alluvial Siltation Engine.

Models catchment geomorphology, bedrock and topsoil incision, and flood-basin alluvial replenishment according to the canonical Stream Power Incision Law (Howard & Kerby 1983; Whipple & Tucker 1999) and Bagnold sediment transport dynamics (Bagnold 1966; Montgomery 2007):

Stream Power Law of Fluvial Erosion: $$\dot{E} = K_{\text{erod}} \cdot A^m \cdot S^n$$ where:

  • $A$: Upstream contributing drainage area ($\text{km}^2$), coupled to the Hack river basin law from ConstructalFlowArchitectureEngine ($L \approx 1.4 A^{0.57}$).
  • $S$: Local topographic slope gradient ($S = |\nabla z|$).
  • $m = 0.5$, $n = 1.0$: Canonical physical stream power exponents.
  • $K_{\text{erod}}$: Soil erodibility coefficient, damped exponentially by vegetative root structure: $$K_{\text{erod}} = K_0 \cdot \exp\left(-\frac{B_{\text{nat}} + B_{\text{agr}}}{B_{\text{ref}}}\right)$$ Anthropogenic deforestation and overgrazing drastically elevate erodibility by an order of magnitude.

Bagnold Lowland Alluvial Deposition & Floodplain Soil Replenishment: When sediment-laden rivers discharge onto flat alluvial lowlands and deltas ($S invalid input: '<' 0.002$), sediment carrying capacity collapses ($\Omega = \rho g Q S \to 0$). The precipitated mineral alluvium replenishes topsoil depth and Soil Organic Carbon (SOC), reproducing the sustainable multi-millennial fertility of ancient hydraulic civilizations (Nile, Tigris-Euphrates, Indus, Yellow River) despite intensive agriculture.
